source.title: Frequency Principle: Fourier Analysis Sheds Light on Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Zhi-Qin John Xu; Yaoyu Zhang; Tao Luo; Yan Xiao; Zheng Ma

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies frequency-dependent training and discusses generalization, but does not test the claim versions about random labels, unstructured inputs, regularization, or the order of learning real and noisy labels.
record.gate_note: The paper's random-label generalization statements are explanations or references to prior work, not results from its own random-label experiments. Its own generalization discussion reports results for MNIST, CIFAR10, and parity, which do not match any listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures convergence of Fourier components on true-label datasets, synthetic functions and a parity task. It does not measure random-label fitting or compare learning real patterns with memorizing noisy labels. Low-frequency-first learning alone does not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the generalization discussion. More broadly, the authors conclude that DNNs often learn low response frequencies first, demonstrate this across architectures and losses, and use this bias to qualitatively explain generalization differences and motivate combining DNN solvers with conventional numerical methods.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies frequency-dependent convergence and Fourier structure, not the original random-label intervention or its training-error and test-error measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes its frequency-principle results across architectures, datasets, and loss functions, but does not show these choices changing a result on the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Fourier analysis distinguishes good generalization on MNIST/CIFAR10 from poor generalization on parity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-frequency bias can help explain generalization differences between low-frequency-dominant image tasks and high-frequency-dominant parity tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Projection and filtering experiments show lower response frequencies converging before higher frequencies on true-label MNIST/CIFAR10 across several architectures and losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DNN training often fits low response frequencies before high response frequencies.

record.problems: The paper states that its high-dimensional Fourier evidence examines selected directions; it also describes the generalization explanation as qualitative. The parity experiment uses 200 randomly selected points in dimension 10.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time for random versus true labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test performance across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of explicit regularization on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels; no such label comparison is performed.

record.verdict_notes: The abstract's reference to randomized datasets is explanatory, not an own-study random-label result. Discussion of noise added to MNIST concerns Rahaman et al.'s work.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and comparison with true labels.
Training time on random versus true labels and convergence versus corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep of random label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: tanh-DNN with widths 784-400-200-10
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated generalization on MNIST using Fourier analysis of the trained network output.
rows.measure: Generalization, described as good; the Fourier transform of the trained output on the full dataset recovers dominant low frequencies.
rows.value: The Fourier transform of the output of a well-trained DNN on the full dataset faithfully recovers the dominant low frequencies; this indicates good generalization.
rows.note: This is a result about true-label MNIST generalization, not random-label fitting or any listed version.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked: true-label MNIST generalization does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: tanh-DNN with widths 10-500-100-1
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated generalization on a parity function using Fourier analysis of the trained network output.
rows.measure: Generalization, described as poor; the trained output's Fourier transform significantly deviates from the parity function's transform at almost all frequencies.
rows.value: The Fourier transform of the output of a well-trained DNN on the training inputs significantly deviates from the parity function's transform at almost all frequencies; this indicates bad generalization.
rows.note: Randomly selected parity examples are not random labels. This result does not test any listed version.
rows.check: Randomly sampled parity examples have deterministic labels. Also, the evaluation domain is inconsistent in the source: Section 7.1 says training inputs, whereas Figure 5's caption says the whole dataset. The row should flag this ambiguity.
